nodeFieldLifts.valueRule: Lift the channel value out of scope and emit NodeSpec.writeChannels: ['<channel>']. Remaining scope keys (if any) produce the canonical ScopeSpec; if scope had only the channel key, scope is omitted entirely (defaults to 'all').
nodeFieldLifts.notes: Channel scoping is a NodeSpec-level write filter (Gap 1, Option B). Plural array because more than one channel can be selected. Empty array means 'no further restriction beyond the descriptor's declared writable channels.'

nodeFieldLifts.valueRule: Direct passthrough as the writeChannels array. Use this when the author wants more than one channel restricted.
nodeFieldLifts.notes: Plural author shape parallels the canonical plural field.

nodeFieldLifts.valueRule: Legacy V2/V3 spelling. 'foreground' → ['foreground'], 'background' → ['background'], 'both' → [] (no restriction; descriptor's declared writable channels apply).
nodeFieldLifts.notes: Default behavior. Override per-alias by setting applyToIsInput: true on the alias entry — that flag tells the canonicalize function to treat applyTo as a per-effect input binding instead of lifting it. shader.focused_row_gradient is the witnessed example: its descriptor declares applyTo as an input that selects which channel the computed gradient color targets. Effects without the flag let applyTo fall through to this lift rule.

shadowFieldRenames.notes: Gap 3 closed. ShadowSpec.edgeCrossingPolicy is optional with three values. The author-side V2/V3 spelling 'edgeCrossing' canonicalizes to the longer field name; values pass through unchanged.

envelopes.authorForm: string from a known enum set

sigils.notes: Binding reference. Fallback resolves from the signal's default value at canonicalize time; the canonicalizer fails fast if the signal id is unresolved.

sigils.expansion: { kind: 'signal', id: '<id>', fallback: <fallback parsed by sibling envelope> }
sigils.notes: Inline fallback override for the signal reference.
